text: To answer these questions, this study utilizes nationally representative data from the 2021 China Social Survey (CSS). Consistent with the definition established above, the analysis focuses on Chinese adults aged 60 and older, a group particularly vulnerable to the psychosocial harms of discriminatory attitudes. Specifically, this study first examines the direct impact of ageism on life satisfaction among older adults, then investigates the mediating roles of leisure and social engagement satisfaction, and finally conducts heterogeneity analyses to assess differential effects across gender and household registration (hukou) types.
source_label: Perceived age discrimination and life satisfaction among older adults in China: mediating roles of leisure and social satisfaction
